assessment.nobel_worthiness: A genuinely new state of matter: the Z2 topological classification and quantum spin Hall effect (Kane-Mele) followed by the HgTe/CdTe edge-channel experiment. It changed how we classify band structures and is exactly the kind of quantum-materials discovery where theory predicts and experiment confirms, with strong links to first-principles materials work.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele supplied the decisive theory (Z2 invariant, spin-orbit-driven quantum spin Hall phase). Molenkamp led the first experimental observation in HgTe quantum wells, following the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang prediction, whose authors are not in the credited names. A Kane-Mele-Molenkamp configuration is defensible but leaves the BHZ prediction and Konig et al. co-authors unrecognised, which I would flag.
assessment.maturity: Mature: nearly two decades of independent confirmation in HgTe, 3D topological insulators (Bi-Sb, Bi2Se3), and a large downstream literature including ab initio materials prediction. Timing is good and the interpretation is stable.
uncertainties: Fair division of credit between Kane-Mele, the BHZ prediction and the 3D topological insulator experiments is not fully settled.
I have not independently verified the details of the early experimental chronology.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Prediction of flat bands at magic twist angles and the discovery of correlated insulators and superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene opened moire quantum materials, a new tunable platform for strongly correlated physics. Original, clear, and a vivid case of experiment confirming a surprising theoretical idea.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer-MacDonald supplied the continuum-model prediction of the magic angle; Jarillo-Herrero's group delivered the 2018 experimental discovery (first-author Yuan Cao is not in the credited names). I would propose MacDonald and Jarillo-Herrero; Bistritzer is a plausible but more junior third. Kaxiras, Santos and others also contributed earlier theory, which raises allocation questions.
assessment.maturity: Fast-maturing: many independent groups reproduced the correlated phases and superconductivity, though mechanism of the superconductivity is still debated. Possibly slightly early, but the experimental base is broad.
uncertainties: The pairing mechanism and the full phase diagram remain debated.
Credit for the early theory versus the experiment, and the role of the unnamed first author, is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Subpicosecond demagnetization of nickel (Beaurepaire 1996) and all-optical magnetic switching (Kimel, Rasing) revealed that spins can be manipulated on timescales far faster than conventional spin-lattice relaxation. This is a deep and still partly unexplained question in non-equilibrium magnetism, and it links to measured spectra from large facilities and to modern ab initio spin dynamics.
assessment.attribution: Beaurepaire is the clear originator of ultrafast demagnetization; Kimel and Rasing led the all-optical switching and antiferromagnetic/ferrimagnetic control. Other contributors (e.g. Stanciu, Hohlfeld, Bigot, Radu, Ostler) are outside the credited list, so the configuration is reasonable but not exhaustive.
assessment.maturity: Phenomenon firmly confirmed by many groups for nearly three decades; the microscopic mechanism (superdiffusive transport versus spin-flip scattering, angular momentum transfer) is still contested, which is a mild concern for a prize citing explanation.
uncertainties: The microscopic mechanism of ultrafast demagnetization is not settled.
Technological impact for magnetic recording is still prospective.
Part of the field is a compound discovery (demagnetization versus helicity-dependent switching) that might need separate treatment.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Discovery of superconductivity in LaFeAsO(F) in 2008 and its rapid raising of Tc above 50 K created a second family of high-temperature superconductors with multiband, magnetically proximate physics, which is rich territory for electronic-structure theory. Importance is high and the discovery is clear-cut.
assessment.attribution: Hosono's group made the initial discovery; Chen and Zhao's groups quickly pushed Tc to the 40-55 K range with rare-earth substitution. Credit is relatively cleanly separable, with Hosono clearly first. Others (e.g. Rotter, Johrendt for 122 compounds) are not credited.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed and extensively studied over 15+ years. The pairing mechanism is still debated and no room-temperature or technological breakthrough followed, so recognition would be for the discovery rather than a solved theory.
uncertainties: Pairing symmetry and mechanism remain unresolved.
Whether the committee regards the cuprate-era recognition as already covering this field.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock concept (magic wavelength, Katori) and its realisation at 10^-18 fractional uncertainty (Ye) is a milestone in precision measurement with real tests of relativity, searches for varying constants and prospects for redefining the second. Clear invention with outstanding quantitative reproducibility.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed and demonstrated the lattice-clock concept; Ye drove it to the 10^-18 regime with strontium and related work. The two-person credit is clean, although the ion-clock community and others (e.g. Ludlow, Hinkley, Bloom contributions) are not credited. This is outside my own subfield, so I defer somewhat.
assessment.maturity: Mature and independently confirmed across several laboratories, with clock comparisons demonstrating the precision. Timely, especially as the redefinition of the second approaches.
uncertainties: The relation to previously recognised frequency comb and ion-trap clock prizes could cause committee debate.
I am not an expert in atomic clocks and have not independently checked the metrology claims.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Metal-halide perovskite solar cells rose in efficiency from a few percent to over 25 percent in little more than a decade and opened a new class of defect-tolerant semiconductors. It combines real sustainable-energy relevance with materials physics I care about, though the central contribution is more a materials-and-device advance than a single fundamental physics discovery.
assessment.attribution: Miyasaka reported the first perovskite-sensitised cell (2009), Park and Snaith drove the solid-state, high-efficiency devices (2012). The credited trio is plausible, but others such as Gratzel, Seok, and Kanatzidis also have strong claims, so allocation is contested.
assessment.maturity: Performance records are widely reproduced, but long-term stability and lead toxicity remain unsolved and commercialisation is incomplete, so the work may be premature for a physics prize.
uncertainties: Stability and scalability are not yet demonstrated.
Whether the committee sees this as physics or chemistry-adjacent materials engineering.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The quantized anomalous Hall effect in magnetically doped topological insulators gives a dissipationless chiral edge state without an external magnetic field. It is a clean, quantitatively precise result bridging magnetism, topology and first-principles prediction, which suits my profile well.
assessment.attribution: Fang, Dai and collaborators predicted the effect in Cr/Mn-doped Bi2Se3-type materials; Xue's group made the 2013 experimental observation in Cr-doped (Bi,Sb)2Te3. Haldane's 1988 model is the conceptual root, and the Haldane contribution has already been recognised, which complicates the narrative.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed independently (including by groups in the US and Germany) and the precision of quantisation has improved, but the effect still requires very low temperatures, and the MnBi2Te4 lineage is still developing.
uncertainties: Dependence on the earlier topological insulator prize narrative and the Haldane precedent.
Unresolved precise allocation between the theory and experiment teams, and other experimental contributors outside the credited list.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Current-induced spin-orbit torques, enabling electrical switching of magnetisation in heavy-metal/ferromagnet bilayers, are a clear physical discovery tied to spin-orbit coupling and interface physics, with real relevance for non-volatile magnetic memory. They fall squarely in the magnetism community I know well.
assessment.attribution: Miron and Gambardella reported the Rashba-type switching in Pt/Co/AlOx (2011) and Buhrman's group demonstrated spin-Hall torque switching (2012). The origin of the torques (spin Hall versus Rashba-Edelstein) and priority among groups, including Ralph and others not credited, make the attribution contested.
assessment.maturity: Rapidly adopted and independently reproduced, with devices under development, but the microscopic mechanism of the torques is still debated and the technology has not yet fully matured.
uncertainties: Disputed microscopic origin and credit between Rashba and spin Hall mechanisms.
Likely overlap with other spintronics recognition, and the incomplete credit list excludes major contributors such as Ralph.
